subject: Neurology
vignette: A developing embryo is exposed to a toxin that selectively destroys the neuroepithelial cells lining the neural tube. At birth, the affected individual would be expected to have the greatest deficiency in which of the following cell types?
question: Loss of neural tube neuroepithelium would most directly deplete which of the following?

options.text: CNS neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and ependymal cells.

explanation_correct: The neuroepithelia of the neural tube give rise to the cells of the central nervous system: CNS neurons and the CNS glial cells, which include astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and ependymal cells. Destroying the neural tube lining therefore depletes all of these populations. Dorsal root ganglion neurons, Schwann cells, and adrenal medullary cells are neural crest derivatives, and microglia come from mesoderm, so they would be relatively spared.

explanation_incorrect.A: Dorsal root ganglion neurons are derived from neural crest cells, not from neural tube neuroepithelium.
explanation_incorrect.B: Schwann cells are peripheral glial cells derived from the neural crest, not from the neural tube.
explanation_incorrect.D: Chromaffin cells of the adrenal medulla are neural crest derivatives and part of the peripheral sympathetic system, not the CNS.
explanation_incorrect.E: Microglia are specialized macrophages derived from mesoderm, not from neural tube neuroepithelium.

educationalObjective: Neural tube neuroepithelium produces CNS neurons and glia (astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, ependymal cells).

subject: Neurology
vignette: A fetus has a defect in the specification and migration of neural crest cells. Which of the following structures would be expected to fail to develop normally as a direct result?
question: Which structure is most likely absent or abnormal due to defective neural crest development?

options.text: Dorsal root ganglia and the adrenal medulla.

explanation_correct: Neural crest cells migrate widely and give rise to PNS neurons, including those of the dorsal root ganglia and autonomic (sympathetic, parasympathetic, and enteric) ganglia, as well as PNS glia (Schwann and satellite cells) and the adrenal medulla. A defect in neural crest specification or migration would therefore disrupt the dorsal root ganglia and adrenal medulla. CNS neurons and glia arise from the neural tube, not the neural crest.

explanation_incorrect.A: Cerebral cortical neurons are CNS neurons derived from neural tube neuroepithelium, not neural crest.
explanation_incorrect.B: Astrocytes are CNS glial cells derived from the neural tube.
explanation_incorrect.C: Ependymal cells line the ventricles and are derived from neural tube neuroepithelium.
explanation_incorrect.E: Oligodendrocytes are the myelinating cells of the CNS and arise from the neural tube, not neural crest.

educationalObjective: Neural crest gives rise to PNS neurons and glia and the adrenal medulla.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A researcher is tracing the embryonic lineage of the resident macrophages of the brain and spinal cord. These cells are not derived from neuroectoderm but instead originate from an embryonic germ layer that also gives rise to the cardiovascular system and blood cells. From which germ layer do these cells originate?
question: From which embryonic tissue are CNS microglia derived?
explanation_correct: Microglia are the specialized macrophages of the CNS, and unlike other CNS glia they are not derived from neuroectoderm. They originate from mesoderm, the germ layer that also produces blood and cardiovascular tissues. This mesodermal origin distinguishes microglia from astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and ependymal cells, all of which arise from neural tube neuroepithelium.

explanation_incorrect.A: Neural tube neuroepithelium gives rise to CNS neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and ependymal cells, but not microglia.
explanation_incorrect.B: Neural crest gives rise to peripheral glia such as Schwann and satellite cells, not the resident macrophages of the CNS.
explanation_incorrect.C: Surface ectoderm contributes to the epidermis and, after induction, the neural plate; it is not the source of microglia.
explanation_incorrect.D: Endoderm gives rise to the linings of the digestive and respiratory tracts and associated organs, not CNS macrophages.

educationalObjective: Microglia are mesoderm-derived macrophages, unlike other CNS glia which are neuroectoderm-derived.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 32-year-old woman presents with a sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy. A nerve biopsy shows demyelination of peripheral axons. The neurologist notes that the cell responsible for peripheral myelination has a different embryonic origin from the cell that myelinates axons within the CNS. Which of the following pairings of a cell and its embryonic origin is correct?
question: Which of the following cell-origin pairings is correct?
explanation_correct: Schwann cells are the myelinating glia of the peripheral nervous system and are derived from the neural crest, as are satellite cells and other PNS glia. In contrast, oligodendrocytes myelinate CNS axons and arise from neural tube neuroepithelium. This difference in origin underlies the differing regenerative capacities of peripheral and central axons. Thus the correct pairing is Schwann cells with neural crest.

explanation_incorrect.A: Oligodendrocytes are CNS myelinating cells derived from neural tube neuroepithelium, not neural crest.
explanation_incorrect.C: Satellite cells are PNS glia derived from neural crest, not mesoderm.
explanation_incorrect.D: Microglia are mesoderm-derived macrophages, not derivatives of neural tube neuroepithelium.
explanation_incorrect.E: Astrocytes are CNS glia derived from neural tube neuroepithelium, not neural crest.

educationalObjective: Schwann cells are neural crest-derived PNS glia, whereas oligodendrocytes are neural tube-derived CNS glia.
